focus: Wiring map, live pre-arm score, and what phases 005-008 already cover
noveltyJustification: All six findings are new to this lineage: the pre-arm rate measures spontaneous doc reads, the live log is incomplete, capped runs distort the denominator, DSH is conditionally wired, host command names differ, and G5 is documented but unfixed.

label: The pre-arm start rate is not a surfacing baseline: phase 005 is unbuilt, so no brief names a command, and started is a document read or COMMAND line rather than a response to an offer.
The dispatched baseline is stale: the live log scores claude 3/12, codex 0/12, pi 0/12, devin 2/12, opencode 5/10, dsh 3/10, with 24/24/24/13/10/10 rows against a planned 24 per runtime.
Capped runs remain in the start denominator (pi 2, devin 4, opencode 4 of the live rows), hiding an unmeasured gap: opencode 5/10 is at best 5/6 and devin 2/12 at best 2/8.
Five runtimes have an in-repo advisor delivery path; DSH's prompt-advisor adapter is disabled unless promptAdvisor:true and no repo-side DSH config enables it.

Codex, Pi and DSH expose flat host prompts named /create-readme while the canonical command is /create:readme; phase 006 covers reading the document but maps no host name and measures no failed host invocation.
G5 is documented but unfixed: .claude/commands/create/skill.md makes Claude list one create skill and hide all twelve sibling create:* commands, and no phase changes the layout.

direction: Hook not wired on most runtimes
reason: Five of six runtimes have a live delivery path, and Codex and Devin proxy the same adapter as Claude.

direction: Hook too slow so the brief is dropped
reason: Measured median hook latency is about 200 ms against a 2500 ms budget and a warm embed is 6.57 ms.
